boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 15:1 opens with the strict word-event formula, וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.15.1), immediately followed by the address בֶּן אָדָ֕ם (oshb:Ezek.15.2) at 15:2, which puts the riddle about the useless vine-wood in the standard oracle-onset frame. Close side: the row's final verse, MT 15:8, ends the applied sentence against Jerusalem's inhabitants and carries the utterance-of-the-Lord-YHWH signature at its own end, matched by a pe mark recorded on 15:8 in the single-witness paragraph layer. A samekh mark sits earlier, on 15:5 (sweep: 8 verses), where the riddle's own question -- whether the vine-wood, even charred, is fit for any use -- reaches its rhetorical dead end before the messenger formula כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.15.6) opens the application at 15:6. That mid-chapter mark is weighed and not adopted as the row seam: the application (15:6-8) answers the riddle (15:1-5) rather than opening an independent formula-bounded unit of its own, and a three-verse application row would not itself carry a fresh word-event onset. The row is therefore kept as the whole chapter, with the internal mark disclosed rather than acted on.

oshb:Ezek.15.5 (disclosure: parashah: samekh recorded on this verse, single-witness; informs but does not by itself set the internal riddle/application seam)

strongest_rejected_alternative: A two-row split at the 15:5/15:6 samekh (the riddle 15:1-5 against its application 15:6-8) was weighed and not taken: the application never opens with its own word-event formula, so a 15:6-8 row would be a three-verse row without the complete-unit exception the over-split guard requires, and it would sever a question from its own answer.

device_notes: Whole-chapter span disclosed under the E-02 cap: MT 15 is 8 verses and is kept as one row rather than split at its internal samekh (15:5, single witness). This span carries no K/Q note, no paseq, and the editorial-note layer is silent across it.

boundary_rationale: Onset side: the word-event formula וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.16.1) at 16:1, the address בֶּן אָדָ֕ם (oshb:Ezek.16.2) at 16:2, and the messenger formula naming the addressee, כֹּה אָמַ֨ר אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ לִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם (oshb:Ezek.16.3) at 16:3, together open the foundling allegory and fix Jerusalem as the figure's referent from the first clause; the pe recorded at MT 15:8 (single witness) closes the unit before it, corroborating this row's onset from the far side of the seam. Close side: MT 16:14 is this row's last verse, and its own final words are the utterance formula נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.16.14), closing the first movement (the abandoned infant clothed, fed and enthroned) before the narrative turns to her unfaithfulness at 16:15. No parashah mark falls between 16:1 and 16:14 (sweep: 14 verses), so the utterance-formula close is the only mark-independent boundary evidence available for this stretch, and it is taken as such. MT 16:13 (oshb:Ezek.16.13) carries a doubled Ketiv/Qere note inside this span: the running text reads the ketiv forms ששי and אכלתי in place of the pointed readings; the Qere layer gives (Qere for both) שֵׁ֤שׁ (fine linen) and אָכָ֑לְתְּ (you ate) respectively. Neither Qere is used to argue this boundary; both are disclosed because the span covers them.

Close side: MT 16:23 closes the row, and its final clause is the double cry and utterance formula א֣וֹי א֣וֹי לָ֔ךְ נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.16.23) ('woe, woe to you, declares the Lord YHWH'), a verse-final close reached after the summary at 16:22 recalls the days of the addressee's youth. No parashah mark falls in this four-verse stretch (sweep: 4 verses); the seam again rests on the verse-final formula alone. Two single Ketiv/Qere notes fall inside this span: MT 16:20 reads (oshb:Ezek.16.20) the ketiv מתזנתך and MT 16:22 reads (oshb:Ezek.16.22) the ketiv זכרתי.

boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 16:24 opens with no fresh formula device, וַתִּבְנִי לָ֖ךְ גֶּ֑ב וַתַּעֲשִׂי לָ֥ךְ רָמָ֖ה בְּכָל רְחֽוֹב (oshb:Ezek.16.24), continuing the word-event unit by default and cataloguing the addressee's promiscuity against Egypt, Philistia, Assyria and Chaldea in turn (16:26-29). Close side: the row is taken through 16:34, whose final clause וַתְּהִ֥י לְהֶֽפֶךְ (oshb:Ezek.16.34) ('and you became the opposite') closes the reversal-of-a-prostitute's-wages figure just before the summons לָכֵ֣ן זוֹנָ֔ה שִׁמְעִ֖י (oshb:Ezek.16.35) ('therefore, prostitute, hear') opens at 16:35. The utterance formula recurs at 16:30, מָ֤ה אֲמֻלָה֙ לִבָּתֵ֔ךְ נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה (oshb:Ezek.16.30), but sits mid-verse there, with the clause on the deeds of a brazen prostitute still to follow, so it is weighed and not treated as a row-final refrain. The paragraph layer records a pe on 16:35, one verse AFTER this row's own close at 16:34, not on 16:34 itself; that is disclosed rather than smoothed over, because it means the mark corroborates a seam one verse later than the addressee-shift onset this row's boundary is actually argued from. MT 16:25 (oshb:Ezek.16.25) carries a single Ketiv/Qere note, reading the ketiv תזנתך in the running text. MT 16:31 (oshb:Ezek.16.31) also carries a doubled Ketiv/Qere note inside this span, one of the five flagged doubled-note verses in this chapter: the running text reads the ketivs עשיתי and הייתי, against the Qere readings עָשִׂ֖ית and הָיִ֥ית (oshb:Ezek.16.31, Qere for both); neither Qere is used to argue this boundary.

boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 16:35, לָכֵ֣ן זוֹנָ֔ה שִׁמְעִ֖י דְּבַר יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.16.35) ('therefore, prostitute, hear the word of YHWH'), is the addressee-change summons the paragraph layer marks with a pe recorded on this same verse; the messenger formula כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֗ה (oshb:Ezek.16.36) completes the introduction at 16:36 and opens the judgment sentence proper. Close side: the row is taken through 16:43, whose own final clause is the plain עַ֖ל כָּל תּוֹעֲבֹתָֽיִךְ (oshb:Ezek.16.43) ('besides all your abominations'), not a formula refrain -- the utterance formula recurs earlier in the same verse but mid-clause, with this tail still to follow, so it is weighed and not used as the close. The close is instead argued from the fresh default onset that follows: MT 16:44, הִנֵּה֙ כָּל הַמֹּשֵׁ֔ל עָלַ֥יִךְ יִמְשֹׁ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר כְּאִמָּ֖ה בִּתָּֽהּ (oshb:Ezek.16.44) ('behold, everyone who quotes proverbs will quote this proverb against you: like mother, like daughter'), opens the sisters figure on its own mashal-label onset, הַמֹּשֵׁ֔ל עָלַ֥יִךְ יִמְשֹׁ֖ל (oshb:Ezek.16.44; mashal sweep: 11 verses), rather than a word-event or messenger formula, so the row is closed at 16:43 before that proverb onset begins. MT 16:43 also carries (oshb:Ezek.16.43) a doubled Ketiv/Qere note: the running text reads the ketivs זכרתי and עשיתי, with the Qere layer giving זָכַרְתְּ֙ (oshb:Ezek.16.43, Qere) and עָשִׂית֙ (oshb:Ezek.16.43, Qere).

boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 17:1 opens (oshb:Ezek.17.1) with the strict word-event formula וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר, and 17:2 names the genre directly, בֶּן אָדָ֕ם ח֥וּד חִידָ֖ה וּמְשֹׁ֣ל מָשָׁ֑ל אֶל בֵּ֖ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Ezek.17.2) ('son of man, propound a riddle and speak a parable to the house of Israel'), before the messenger formula כֹּה אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה (oshb:Ezek.17.3) opens the eagle-and-vine figure itself. Close side: this row runs through 17:10, whose concluding clause תִּיבַ֣שׁ יָבֹ֔שׁ (oshb:Ezek.17.10) ('it will surely wither') answers the riddle's own rhetorical question, matched by a pe recorded on this same verse in the single-witness paragraph layer -- the riddle's content is complete and the mark coincides with it, so the row is closed here before the interpretation opens with its own word-event formula at 17:11.

boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 18:10 opens with no formula device, the whole verse וְהוֹלִ֥יד בֵּן פָּרִ֖יץ שֹׁפֵ֣ךְ דָּ֑ם וְעָ֣שָׂה אָ֔ח מֵאַחַ֖ד מֵאֵֽלֶּה (oshb:Ezek.18.10) ('and he fathers a violent son who sheds blood'), continuing the case-law series by default. The righteous grandson's case (18:14) and the summary restatement (18:19-20) follow without any fresh formula onset of their own, since 18:18 explicitly recalls the father's own guilt from 18:10-13 before drawing the general rule -- one continuous legal argument across three generations, not three independently onset units. Close side: the row runs through 18:20; its opening clause הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַחֹטֵ֖את הִ֣יא תָמ֑וּת בֵּ֞ן לֹא יִשָּׂ֣א בַּעֲוֺ֣ן הָאָ֗ב (oshb:Ezek.18.20) ('the soul who sins shall die; a son shall not bear his father's iniquity') restates 18:4's thesis and closes the argument, matched by a samekh recorded on this same verse.

oshb:Ezek.18.13 (disclosure: content-final close of the wicked son's case alone, weighed and not used as a row seam because 18:14 explicitly continues the same father-son chain)

boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 18:21 opens with no formula device, וְהָרָשָׁ֗ע כִּ֤י יָשׁוּב֙ (oshb:Ezek.18.21) ('but if the wicked turns'), a default onset for the repentance case; the running text reads the ketiv חטאתו (oshb:Ezek.18.21) in place of the pointed form. The oath-adjacent utterance formula sits mid-verse there ('declares the Lord YHWH'), with the rhetorical question's own final clause, 'and not rather that he should turn from his way and live', still to follow; the samekh mark closes the whole verse regardless of the formula's mid-verse position, and it is that mark, not formula-finality, that is used as the close evidence here.

boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 18:27 opens with no formula device, וּבְשׁ֣וּב רָשָׁ֗ע מֵֽרִשְׁעָתוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.18.27) ('again, when a wicked person turns from the wickedness he has committed'), the positive repentance case answering 18:24-26; the running text reads the ketiv וישוב (oshb:Ezek.18.28) at 18:28. Israel's objection recurs at 18:29 in a form the OSHB editors flag with a single-witness note against BHS. The judgment proper then opens at 18:30 with לָכֵן֩ אִ֨ישׁ כִּדְרָכָ֜יו אֶשְׁפֹּ֤ט אֶתְכֶם֙ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה (oshb:Ezek.18.30) ('therefore I will judge you, each according to his ways, O house of Israel, declares the Lord YHWH'). boundary_rationale: Onset side: the pe recorded at MT 18:32 (single witness) closes the preceding unit before it, corroborating this row's onset from the far side of the seam; MT 19:1 itself opens with the distinct qinah-command onset וְאַתָּה֙ שָׂ֣א קִינָ֔ה אֶל נְשִׂיאֵ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Ezek.19.1) ('and you, take up a lamentation for the princes of Israel') -- not a word-event formula and not a son-of-man address, but the genre-naming command proper to a lament. Close side: the row runs to the chapter's own colophon, MT 19:14, the whole verse וַתֵּצֵ֨א אֵ֜שׁ מִמַּטֵּ֤ה בַדֶּ֨יהָ֙ פִּרְיָ֣הּ אָכָ֔לָה וְלֹא הָ֥יָה בָ֛הּ מַטֵּה עֹ֖ז שֵׁ֣בֶט לִמְשׁ֑וֹל קִ֥ינָה הִ֖יא וַתְּהִ֥י לְקִינָֽה (oshb:Ezek.19.14), whose last clause names its own genre a second time ('this is a lamentation, and it is used as a lamentation'), matched by a pe recorded on this same verse. A pe also falls mid-chapter, on 19:9, at the close of the lion-cubs figure (אֲרָי֖וֹת, oshb:Ezek.19.2) -- לְמַ֗עַן לֹא יִשָּׁמַ֥ע קוֹל֛וֹ ע֖וֹד אֶל הָרֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Ezek.19.9) ('so that his voice should no more be heard on the mountains of Israel') -- immediately before the second figure opens at 19:10, אִמְּךָ֥ כַגֶּ֛פֶן בְּדָמְךָ֖ עַל מַ֣יִם שְׁתוּלָ֑ה (oshb:Ezek.19.10) ('your mother was like a vine in your vineyard, planted by the water'). That internal mark is disclosed and weighed, not adopted as a row seam: the colophon at 19:14 names the whole composition, both figures together, a single lamentation, so the span is kept as one row rather than split at its own internal parashah break.
